passages.grammar: Verse 1 is a nominal analysis: prameyam is qualified by svatantram, paratantram, and dvividham; matam is a kta resultative. Verse 13 correlates relative ya with saḥ; jānāti governs the iti-content. The source’s saṃsārān before mucyate is the optional nasalized sandhi form of underlying saṃsārāt before m (Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.4.45). The transmitted ya is retained rather than normalized to yaḥ/yo ’.

grammar_annotations.label: relative ya with saḥ
grammar_annotations.note: The relative pronoun ya (‘whoever’) is paired with saḥ (‘that one/he’): ‘whoever …, that person …’. This is Sanskrit’s standard relative–correlative construction.

grammar_annotations.label: saṃsārān
grammar_annotations.note: The transmitted continuous-text form before mucyate. It represents the underlying ablative saṃsārāt (‘from saṃsāra’) through the optional nasalized sandhi described in the note.

grammar_annotations.label: saṃsārāt
grammar_annotations.note: The underlying ablative form means ‘from saṃsāra.’ Before m it may appear in continuous text as saṃsārān through the optional nasalized sandhi noted here.

grammar_annotations.label: transmitted ya
grammar_annotations.note: ya is the reading of this textual witness. The reader reports it rather than changing it to the more familiar nominative forms yaḥ or yo ’.

grammar_annotations.label: yaḥ/yo ’
grammar_annotations.note: These are normalized nominative forms of the relative pronoun: yaḥ before a consonant or pause, yo ’ before a vowel. The edition instead transmits ya, so the reader preserves that witness rather than silently emending it.

passages.devanagari: यथैवाग्न्यादयः शब्दाः प्रवर्तन्ते जनार्दने । तथा निरुक्तिं वक्ष्यामो ज्ञानिनां ज्ञानसिद्धये ॥

passages.grammar: The first half makes agnyādayaḥ śabdāḥ the subject of pravartante; janārdane is a locative marking the person to whom the words apply. Yathā … tathā is the standard correlative construction. In the second half niruktim is the object of vakṣyāmaḥ, jñānasiddhaye is a dative of purpose, and jñāninām is a genitive dependent on siddhi.
